newsitem.title: USA: Haitian junta boss to face drug charges in U.S.
newsitem.headline: Haitian junta boss to face drug charges in U.S.

text.p: The feared former police chief of Haiti's capital was expected to be extradited to the United States on Monday to face charges that he ran a smuggling ring with Colombian drug cartels, local media reported on Sunday.
Lieutenant Colonel Joseph Michel Francois was arrested on Friday by authorities in Honduras on an indictment unveiled by the U.S. Attorney's Office in Miami.

It accused Francois, a leader of the coup that ousted former Haitian President Jean-Bertrand Aristide in 1991, of using Haiti's military regime to ship 33 tonnes of cocaine and heroin to the United States.
The Sun-Sentinel of Fort Lauderdale reported that Francois was to be extradited on Saturday but authorities were unable to get him on the last flight out of Honduras that day.

Francois sought asylum in Honduras last year after being arrested in the Dominican Republic on charges of plotting against the Haitian government. Haiti and the Dominican Republic are neighbours on the Caribbean island of Hispaniola.

Francois, said to be the mastermind of the coup against Aristide, developed a network of plainclothes policemen, or "attaches", who terrorised opponents of the military regime. Aristide was restored to office in 1994 by U.S. troops.
Haitian justice officials said on Friday they would seek the return of the former Port-au-Prince police chief to face charges of murder and other human rights abuses.
The U.S. indictment said the network operated from 1987 until September last year.
Francois was expected to appear in Miami federal court on Monday along with eight co-defendants.
